title: Das Bürle im Himmel
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 167. Text from Wikisource („Das Bürle im Himmel (1857)“, twice proofread against the original). Fresh translation made directly from the German; 1857 spelling preserved exactly. This tale is in Swiss German (Alemannic) dialect; the glossary gives the High German equivalent for each dialect form.
about: A short, wry tale in Swiss dialect: a poor peasant dies and comes to the gate of heaven at the same time as a rich lord, who is welcomed with music while the peasant is let in quietly and without ceremony. “Bürle” is a diminutive of Bauer, “peasant” or “farmer,” and the tale's small joke turns on that smallness: heaven, St. Peter explains, gets a poor man like him every day, and a rich man only once in a hundred years.

sentences.t: S isch emol es arms fromms Bürle gstorbe, und chunt do vor d’ Himmelspforte.
sentences.l: It is once a poor pious little-peasant died, and comes then before the gate of heaven.
sentences.i: Once upon a time a poor pious little peasant died, and came before the gate of heaven.
sentences.n: The whole tale is printed in Swiss German (Alemannic), so nearly every word stands a little aside from the High German of the rest of the collection; the glossary gives the High German equivalent for each form. Here: S isch = es ist, emol = einmal, es = ein (the neuter article, not the pronoun es), arms fromms = armes frommes, gstorbe = gestorben, chunt = kommt, do = da, d’ = die. Two habits begin at once and never stop — the perfect doing the work of the simple past, “ist gestorben” where the north would write “starb”, and Alemannic ch- for High German k-, chunt for kommt.

sentences.t: Zur gliche Zit isch au e riche riche Herr do gsi und het au i Himmel welle.
sentences.l: At the same time is also a rich rich lord there been and has also into heaven wanted.
sentences.i: At the same hour a rich, rich gentleman was there too, and he wanted to get into heaven as well.
sentences.n: gliche = gleichen, Zit = Zeit — Alemannic keeps a plain i where High German has ei. au = auch, not the cry “ow”; e = ein, gsi = gewesen, i Himmel = in den Himmel, welle = gewollt. The doubled riche riche is the dialect piling the word on itself: rich, rich indeed.

sentences.t: Do chunt der heilige Petrus mitem Schlüssel und macht uf und lot der Herr ine;
sentences.l: Then comes the holy Peter with-the key and makes open and lets the lord in;
sentences.i: Then Saint Peter came with the key, opened up and let the gentleman in;
sentences.n: mitem = mit dem, uf = auf (macht uf = macht auf, opens up), lot = lässt, ine = hinein. der Herr stands where High German would have den Herrn: Alemannic has largely given up marking the accusative on the article.

sentences.t: das Bürle het er aber, wies schint, nid gseh und macht d’ Pforte ämel wieder zue.
sentences.l: the little-peasant has he however, as it seems, not seen and makes the gate anyway again shut.
sentences.i: but the little peasant, it seems, he did not see, and he shut the gate again.
sentences.n: wies = wie es, schint = scheint, nid = nicht, gseh = gesehen, zue = zu (macht zue = macht zu). ämel is a flavouring word with no single English equivalent, something like “anyway, at any rate”. wieder here is plain wieder, again — elsewhere in the collection the spelling wider means the preposition, against.

sentences.t: Do het das Bürle vorusse ghört wie de Herr mit alle Freude im Himmel uf gno worde isch, und wie se drin musiziert und gsunge händ.
sentences.l: Then has the little-peasant outside heard how the lord with all joy in heaven up-taken been is, and how they inside made-music and sung have.
sentences.i: Then from outside the little peasant heard how the gentleman had been received into heaven with every joy, and how they were making music and singing within.
sentences.n: vorusse = draußen, ghört = gehört, uf gno worde isch = aufgenommen worden ist, from aufnehmen, to receive; se = sie, drin = drinnen, händ = haben — the Alemannic third person plural, not das Händ, hands. musizieren is to make music, to play; English has no single verb for it.

sentences.t: Ändle isch es do wider still worde, und der heilig Petrus chunt, macht d’ Himmelspforte uf un lot das Bürle au ine.
sentences.l: At last is it then again still become, and the holy Peter comes, makes the gate-of-heaven open and lets the little-peasant in too.
sentences.i: At last it grew quiet again, and Saint Peter came, opened the gate of heaven and let the little peasant in as well.
sentences.n: Ändle = endlich, wider = wieder, again; still worde = still geworden, un = und. heilig stands uninflected where High German writes der heilige Petrus — the dialect drops endings the standard language keeps.

sentences.t: S Bürle het do gmeint s werd jetzt au musiziert und gsunge, wenn es chöm, aber do isch alles still gsi;
sentences.l: The little-peasant has then supposed it would now also be made-music and sung, when it came, but then has everything still been;
sentences.i: The little peasant supposed there would be music and singing for him too when he came in, but everything was silent;
sentences.n: gmeint = gemeint, here in its everyday sense of thought, supposed; s werd = es werde, the subjunctive of reported speech; chöm = käme; gsi = gewesen. es wird musiziert und gsunge is an impersonal passive with no subject at all — German can say “it is being made-music and sung”, English cannot, so the idiomatic line has to supply “there would be music and singing”. The peasant is es, it, because Bürle is neuter.

sentences.t: me hets frile mit aller Liebe ufgno, und d’ Ängele sind em egäge cho, aber gsunge het niemer (niemand).
sentences.l: one has it indeed with all love received, and the angels are toward-him come, but sung has nobody (nobody).
sentences.i: They received him kindly enough, with all love, and the angels came out to meet him, but nobody sang.
sentences.n: The round brackets around niemand are the Grimms’ own, printed in the 1857 text to gloss the Swiss niemer for readers outside Switzerland; round brackets in these tales are always theirs, never ours. me = man, hets = hat es, frile = freilich, ufgno = aufgenommen, Ängele = Engel, em = ihm, egäge = entgegen, cho = gekommen.

sentences.t: Do frogt das Bürle der heilig Petrus worum das me be im nid singe wie be dem riche Herr, s geu, schints, do im Himmel au parteiisch zue wie uf der Erde.
sentences.l: Then asks the little-peasant the holy Peter why that one with him not sings as with the rich lord — it goes, it seems, here in heaven just as partially as on the earth.
sentences.i: Then the little peasant asked Saint Peter why nobody sang for him as they had for the rich gentleman — things went as unfairly in heaven, it seemed, as on earth.
sentences.n: worum das = warum dass; Alemannic keeps a dass after the question word where High German drops it. be = bei, im = ihm — and four words later, in do im Himmel, the same two letters are in dem. singe and geu are subjunctives of reported speech, schints = scheint’s, and zuegoh = zugehen: es geht … zu is how German says “things go on, things are done”. parteiisch is taking sides, showing favour.

sentences.t: Do säit der heilig Petrus „nai wäger, du bisch is so lieb wie alle andere und muesch alle himmlische Freude gniesse wie de rich Herr,
sentences.l: Then says the holy Peter “no truly, you are to-us as dear as all the others and must enjoy every heavenly joy like the rich lord,
sentences.i: Then Saint Peter said: “No, truly — you are as dear to us as any of the others, and you shall enjoy every joy of heaven just as the rich gentleman does;
sentences.n: säit = sagt, nai = nein, bisch = bist, muesch = musst, gniesse = genießen, de = der. wäger is a Swiss word of asseveration, truly, in good earnest. is = uns, us — a trap of the kind a dialect tale sets constantly, since the same two letters spell something quite different in other parts of the collection.

sentences.t: aber lueg, so arme Bürle, wie du äis bisch, chömme alle Tag e Himmel, so ne riche Herr aber chunt nume alle hundert Johr öppe äine.“
sentences.l: but look, poor little-peasants such as you one are, come every day into heaven, but such a rich lord — about one comes only every hundred years.”
sentences.i: but look: poor little peasants such as you come into heaven every day, whereas of rich gentlemen only about one comes in a hundred years.”
sentences.n: lueg = schau, the imperative of luege, to look; äis = eines — wie du äis bisch is literally “as you are one”, such a one as you are; chömme = kommen, e Himmel = in den Himmel (e does duty for both ein and in), ne = ein, nume = nur, Johr = Jahre, öppe = etwa, about. The last clause breaks off and begins again: so ne riche Herr is set up as though it were the subject and is then taken up by äine, one — a shape spoken German falls into and written German avoids. Peter never denies the peasant’s charge; he only does the arithmetic.

glossary.au: auch — also, too (Swiss German (Alemannic); not the cry ‘ow’)
glossary.be: bei — at, with, in the house of (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.bürle: das Bürle — Bäuerlein, little peasant (Swiss German (Alemannic) diminutive of Bauer)
glossary.d: d’ = die, der, das — the (the article reduced to a single letter before its noun; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.do: da, dort; dann — there; then (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.e: ein; in — a, an; also in (‘e Himmel’ = in den Himmel; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.es: ein; es — a, an (the neuter article: ‘es arms Bürle’ = ein armes Bäuerlein); also es, it (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.frogt: fragen — asks (3rd sg. present, fragt; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.ghört: hören — heard (past participle, gehört; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.gliche: gleich — same (inflected, gleichen; ‘zur gliche Zit’ = zur gleichen Zeit; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.het: haben — has (3rd sg. present, hat; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.händ: haben — have (3rd pl. present, haben; Swiss German (Alemannic); not das Händ, hands)
glossary.i: in; ich — in (‘i Himmel’ = in den Himmel); also ich, I (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.im: ihm; in dem — (to) him (‘be im’ = bei ihm); also in dem (‘do im Himmel’) (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.ine: hinein — in, inside (‘lot ne ine’ = lässt ihn hinein; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.is: uns; es — us (‘mit is’ = mit uns); also es, it (Swiss German (Alemannic); not a form of sein)
glossary.isch: sein — is (3rd sg. present, ist; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.johr: das Jahr — years (pl., Jahre; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.liebe: die Liebe — love (‘mit aller Liebe’ = with all love)
glossary.lueg: luege — look! (imperative sg., schau!; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.macht: machen — makes, opens (3rd sg. present; ‘macht uf’ = macht auf, ‘macht zue’ = macht zu)
glossary.ne: ein, eine — a, an (reduced; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.s: es; das — it; the (the pronoun or article clipped to a single letter; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.so: so — so, thus; also ‘such (a)’ before an adjective or an article (‘so arme Bürle wie du’ = so arme Bäuerlein wie du; ‘so ne riche Herr’ = so ein reicher Herr)
glossary.uf: auf — on, up; also the particle of aufmachen and aufnehmen (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.welle: wollen — wanted (past participle, gewollt; ‘het i Himmel welle’ = hat in den Himmel gewollt; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.werd: werden — would be (3rd sg. subjunctive, werde; here the auxiliary of the passive; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.wider: wieder — again (Swiss German (Alemannic) spelling; not wider, against)
glossary.worde: werden — become, been (past participle, geworden/worden; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.zue: zu — to, toward; also the particle of zumachen (‘macht zue’) and zugehen (‘es geht zue’) (Swiss German (Alemannic))
